# Mean BMI Across NHANES Cycles

## Audience Question

For a public-health analyst preparing a briefing: among adults age 20-80 in
the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset, how does mean BMI vary
across cycles for the selected income group?

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# AI prompt: "Load the prepared NHANES classroom CSV from a repository-relative path for a Quarto dashboard."
# Verified: the committed CSV exists at the first candidate path when rendered from the repository root; required columns include Age, BMI, Cycle, and IncomeGroup.
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Control

In this static dashboard, replace `selected_income` with one of these exact
groups: `Low Income (<1.3)`, `Middle Income`, or `High Income (>3.5)`, then
render the document again. The table and figure update to that group; no
interactive dropdown is embedded in this page.

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
# AI prompt: "Show the available income groups and define one editable default value for a static Quarto dashboard."
# Verified: the CSV contains Low Income (<1.3), Middle Income, and High Income (>3.5); the default is one of those values.
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
 selected_income <- "Low Income (<1.3)"

if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
# AI prompt: "Summarize unweighted mean BMI and sample count by NHANES cycle for the selected income group among adults age 20-80, excluding missing BMI or cycle."
# Verified: filters, grouping, mean calculation, and rounding match the unchanged starter analysis; table values are aggregate counts and means.
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(dashboard_summary)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
# AI prompt: "Plot the selected group's mean BMI by NHANES cycle with points connected in cycle order; use a descriptive title, wrap the source/exclusion/limitation caption, and disclose a 24-point viewing window without changing summary values."
# Verified: plot uses only the existing summary, with no smoother or new calculation; coord_cartesian changes only the view, and the wrapped caption discloses source, cohort, exclusions, axis start, and descriptive limits.
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2f6f73") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = "#2f6f73") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(24, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Mean BMI across NHANES cycles:", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = str_wrap("Unweighted mean BMI from the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV; adults age 20-80. Missing BMI, income, cycle, or age and out-of-range ages are excluded. Axis starts at 24. Not a national estimate or evidence of causation.", width = 105)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

## Interpretation

For the selected income group, the table and figure describe mean BMI across
the available NHANES cycles. Use the pattern to guide questions about timing
and context; these descriptive summaries do not explain why values differ.

## Limitation

This unweighted summary does not account for the NHANES survey design, is not a
national estimate, and cannot establish that income causes differences in BMI.
